basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment affects 4/4. Isolated ocular and skeletal reports do not establish >=30%; atopic dermatitis is a separate condition.

decisions.ocular: none: cataract/high myopia reported in one assessed patient; >=30% prevalence is not established across the syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: none: atopic dermatitis in 2/2 assessed patients does not establish direct skin damage from this neurodevelopmental syndrome.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis and foot deformity are isolated reports; small assessed denominators do not establish >=30% prevalence.

basis: Renal anomalies and developmental impairment define disease; contractures/craniosynostosis and night blindness are annotated 80-99%. Hearing impairment is 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: contractures and craniosynostosis are annotated 80-99%; skeletal injury qualifies, while overgrowth alone does not establish a primary locomotor disorder.

basis: Congenital neuromuscular dysfunction, extensive contractures and developmental impairment define disease. Ptosis in only 2 assessed patients does not establish >=30% prevalence.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis is reported in 2/2 assessed patients within a series of at least 10; this limited sampling does not establish common ocular dysfunction.

basis: Machupo infection is defined by hemorrhagic dysfunction and neurologic manifestations, including encephalopathic injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurologic manifestations are explicitly part of the disease definition; the primary tier does not require a separate >=30% estimate.

basis: Androgen resistance defines the endocrine disorder. Hypospadias is a urethral malformation, annotated 30-79% and perineal hypospadias 5/5; urethra belongs to renal.

decisions.renal: involved: frequent hypospadias directly affects urethral anatomy (30-79%; perineal form 5/5); the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Congenital infection with a defining triad of chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus and intracranial calcifications. Hepatic, blood and hearing abnormalities are annotated 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: hydrocephalus and intracranial calcifications are defining diagnostic features, supported by CNS disease ancestry despite occasional frequencies.
decisions.ocular: primary: chorioretinitis is part of the classic diagnostic triad; retinal abnormalities are additionally annotated 80-99%.

basis: Renal tubular transport disorder defined by hyperkalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and hypertension; hypertension is typically early and severe in CUL3 disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is a defining diagnostic feature of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 2, particularly prominent in CUL3 disease.

basis: Metabolic myopathy and optic atrophy define disease; leukoencephalopathy is a defining CNS feature qualifying by the diagnostic exception. Supplied HPO frequencies conflict with the phenotype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: defining leukoencephalopathy qualifies by the diagnostic-feature exception; three primary slots retain metabolic myopathy and optic atrophy.
decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is explicitly syndrome-defining; the inconsistent 1-4% annotation does not negate its primary status.

basis: Renal amyloid causes progressive dysfunction. Hepatic and pulmonary deposits commonly lack functional injury; elevated liver enzymes occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acquired LECT2 amyloid deposition does not itself establish an endocrine or metabolic disorder; proteostasis ancestry alone is insufficient.

basis: Axonal motor-sensory neuropathy defines disease; persistent distal muscle wasting and associated deformity affect most symptomatic patients (>30%) and are intrinsic disease manifestations.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic denervation causes lasting distal muscle loss and deformity in most symptomatic patients (>30%); these are intrinsic manifestations, not separate diseases.
